7138: OBJECTIVES: To characterize the clinical, functional, and educational characteristics of adolescents with myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS) and compare selected illness domains with adults in the Multi-Site Clinical Assessment of ME/CFS (MCAM) study. STUDY DESIGN: Baseline cross-sectional data from adolescents aged 10-17 years enrolled in MCAM were analyzed. Standardized measures included the Short Form-36 (SF-36v2), CDC Symptom Inventory (CDC-SI), Multidimensional Fatigue Inventory (MFI-20), and selected domains of the DePaul Questionnaire. Descriptive statistics characterized the pediatric cohort and bivariate analyses compared adolescents with adults enrolled in MCAM. RESULTS: Forty adolescents (mean age 15.3 years; 52.5% female) were included. Mean illness duration was 4.0 years. Educational disruption was substantial: 64% received homebound or homeschool instruction, 89% missed school because of illness, and participants missed a mean of 10.8 school days during the preceding month. Physical health-related quality of life was substantially impaired. Persistent post-exertional malaise (PEM), unrefreshing sleep, fatigue, and neurocognitive symptoms were common. Compared with adults (n = 595), adolescents had shorter illness duration and better physical functioning, vitality, and social functioning, whereas mental health scores were similar. Adults reported greater burden across several physical symptom domains although many between-group differences were small. CONCLUSIONS: Adolescents with ME/CFS experience substantial multisystem symptom burden, impaired physical functioning and educational disruption. Many core clinical features were similar to those in adults, supporting the need for early recognition and appropriate clinical and educational support.
7139: Background Fatigue is the most prevalent and one of the most disabling symptoms of Functional Neurological Disorder (FND), yet its causal relationship to the condition remains poorly understood. Emerging evidence suggests that chronic fatigue may precede rather than follow the onset of functional neurological symptoms. We hypothesised that a specific phenotype of chronic fatigue, resembling that seen in Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome (ME/CFS), may act as a precipitating factor in FND. Methods We conducted a retrospective review of clinical records from 89 patients assessed through an integrated ME/CFS and FND community service in Wigan, UK, between March 2022 and March 2025. Complete data were available for 76 patients. Fatigue prevalence, phenotype, and its temporal relationship to the onset of FND symptoms were extracted and analysed descriptively. Results Fatigue was reported by 62 of 76 patients (81.5%). In 39 patients (51% of the cohort), fatigue predated the onset of FND symptoms by months to years and exhibited features resembling ME/CFS, including post-exertional malaise, cognitive dysfunction, pain, and immune-like symptoms unrelieved by rest. In all 39, fatigue onset followed one or more stressful life events. A further 23 patients (30%) reported fatigue emerging concurrently with or following FND onset, also with post-exertional exacerbation. The remaining 14 patients (18.5%) without significant fatigue tended to present with isolated focal symptoms and minimal fluctuation, or with primary psychiatric or pain co-morbidities. Conclusions These findings suggest that ME/CFS-like fatigue may play a previously underappreciated precipitating and perpetuating role in a substantial subgroup of FND patients. One possible interpretation is that persistent fatigue and post-exertional symptom exacerbation may constrain the brain’s capacity to process and integrate information, potentially contributing to the emergence or persistence of functional neurological symptoms. These observations are preliminary and require prospective validation, but they raise important questions about FND phenotypic heterogeneity and the appropriateness of exercise-based interventions in fatigue-predominant presentations.
7141: Summary Das Post-Covid-Syndrom (PCS) ist ein heterogener, teilweise schwer beeinträchtigender Multisystemzustand. Fatigue, Belastungsintoleranz, kognitive Störungen, Dyspnoe, Schmerzen, Schlafstörungen und autonome Beschwerden können in wechselnden Kombinationen auftreten. Bei einem Teil der Betroffenen bestehen Post-Exertional Malaise (PEM), ein posturales orthostatisches Tachykardiesyndrom (POTS) oder ein ME/CFS-ähnlicher bzw. ME/CFS-kompatibler Phänotyp. Als mögliche Krankheitsmechanismen werden u a. Viruspersistenz bzw. persistierende Antigene, dysregulierte Immunantworten, Autoimmunphänomene, Endothel- und Gerinnungsveränderungen, Störungen des autonomen Nervensystems, Veränderungen des Mikrobioms sowie des zellulären Energiestoffwechsels diskutiert. Persistierende niedriggradige Immunaktivierung lässt sich dabei als ein verbindendes Modell verstehen; sie ist jedoch weder bei allen Erkrankten nachweisbar noch derzeit durch einen einzelnen klinisch validierten Biomarker erfassbar. Psychosozialer Distress ist ein prospektiv belegter Risikofaktor; autonome Dysregulation ist als mechanistischer Kofaktor bzw. Phänotyp plausibel – ohne dass PCS damit eine somatisierte oder psychogene Störung wäre. Für die Praxis bleibt PCS eine klinische Diagnose, die eine strukturierte Differenzialdiagnostik und eine Phänotypisierung voraussetzt. Zytokinprofile, GPCR-Autoantikörper, sog. Microclot-Tests, kommerzielle Mikrobiomanalysen oder Zonulinbestimmungen besitzen aktuell keinen gesicherten Stellenwert in der Routinediagnostik. Therapeutisch stehen Aufklärung, PEM-gerechtes Belastungsmanagement, Behandlung von Dysautonomie, Schlaf, Schmerz und weiteren Organsymptomen sowie die Korrektur belegter Mangelzustände im Vordergrund. Für keine krankheitsmodifizierende antivirale oder immunmodulatorische Strategie ist bislang eine konsistent bestätigte Wirksamkeit bei etabliertem PCS belegt; für Nirmatrelvir/Ritonavir, therapeutischen Plasmaaustausch und Immunadsorption liegen negative randomisierte Daten vor. Stress- und autonomieregulierende Ansätze wie Herzratenvariabilitäts-Biofeedback oder transkutane Vagusnervstimulation werden als risikoarme Ergänzungen geprüft. Integrativmedizinische Maßnahmen können diese Versorgung ergänzen, müssen jedoch indikationsbezogen, individuell dosiert und evaluierbar eingesetzt werden. Am Krankenhaus für Naturheilweisen (KfN) ist die milde bis moderate Ganzkörperhyperthermie ein wichtiger Baustein des multimodalen stationären Konzepts. Die langjährige klinische Erfahrung, eine hauseigene Beobachtungsstudie und erste externe Daten ergeben ein ermutigendes, aber noch nicht kausal beweisendes Signal. Auch intravenöses Vitamin C wird bei ausgewählten Patienten unter definierten Sicherheitsvoraussetzungen eingesetzt. Entscheidend ist eine transparente Trennung zwischen publizierter Evidenz, eigener klinischer Erfahrung und individualisiertem Therapieversuch.
7146: BACKGROUND: Fatigue is a frequent and disabling symptom across many physical and mental health conditions. Despite similar phenomenology, research has largely focused on single conditions using heterogeneous assessments, limiting cross-condition comparability. This study examines fatigue-related symptom burden across diverse clinical conditions within a shared framework. METHODS: In this multicenter cross-sectional study, adult outpatients (18-65 years) were recruited at five German university hospitals into seven cohorts: chronic primary pain, multiple sclerosis, cancer, chronic renal failure, inflammatory bowel disease, post-COVID condition, and chronic fatigue syndrome. Fatigue was assessed using established self-report measures, including the Fatigue Severity Scale and the Chalder Fatigue Scale, alongside mental health measures. Group differences were analyzed using ANOVA and chi-square tests with adjusted post hoc comparisons. RESULTS: A total of 538 patients were included. Fatigue burden varied substantially across cohorts, with a largely consistent pattern across assessment instruments. Despite significant overall between-cohort differences, the post-COVID (n = 91), chronic primary pain (n = 110), and cancer (n = 124) cohorts showed comparable fatigue levels across several assessment instruments. Multiple sclerosis (n = 63) showed intermediate levels, whereas inflammatory bowel disease (n = 95) consistently showed the lowest fatigue burden. Due to the small sample size, chronic renal failure (n = 30) and chronic fatigue syndrome (n = 25) were analyzed descriptively. Across cohorts, fatigue and most psychological and somatic symptom measures were elevated relative to population reference values. CONCLUSIONS: Using a harmonized assessment framework across seven diagnostic cohorts, this study demonstrates meaningful differences in fatigue burden, with convergent patterns across instruments. The findings provide a reference for contextualizing fatigue severity across conditions and support future hypothesis-driven and mechanistic analyses.
7147: It is usually assumed that patient and doctor know strictly different things: the patient knows the phenomenological aspects of their illness, and the doctor knows its medical aspects. I present a case study, that of myalgic encephalomyelitis, wherein, due to severely dysfunctional institutional knowledge production and transmission mechanisms, the medical aspects of the illness are on the whole better understood by sick people than by their doctors. Indeed, lay scientists within the patient community disseminate and produce science on their disease, ensuring that patients as a whole have reliable knowledge about their disease. By contrast, systemically produced and systemically maintained ignorance on the part of medical professionals is the norm, and may be beyond the specific case study I present.
7148: Abstract Patients severely affected by post-COVID-19 condition (PCC) and myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS) exhibit reduced physical capacity, hyperventilation, and a high susceptibility to post-exertional malaise (PEM). Cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) is considered the gold standard for objectively assessing physical capacity and for exploring underlying physiological limitations. However, evidence regarding the safety and PEM-associated symptoms following CPET remains limited. This study aims to objectively assess physical capacity using CPET, and to systematically investigate changes in PEM-associated symptom duration and severity before and after CPET. 18 PCC patients and 18 healthy controls (matched for sex, age, and body-mass-index) completed a single maximal symptom-limited CPET on a bicycle ergometer. Ten PEM-specific symptoms were assessed daily for 7 days before and 14 days after CPET (scale 0-10). For clinical characterization, the Canadian Consensus Criteria (CCC), Bell Disability Scale, and DePaul Symptom Questionnaire Short-Form-PEM (DSQ-PEM) questionnaires were completed once before the CPET. Among PCC patients, 61% fulfilled ME/CFS criteria, 67% screened positive for DSQ-PEM, and the mean Bell-Score was 37.8 ± 19.3. Physical capacity was markedly reduced compared with healthy controls (Peak power output: 1.1 vs. 2.4 W/kg, p 30, p = 0.276), or ME/CFS status (p = 0.523). Severely affected PCC patients showed markedly reduced physical capacity compared with matched controls. A single maximal but symptom-limited CPET induced only a transient, clinically non-relevant symptom increase (1-3 days) without prolonged exacerbation. Furthermore, the results of the CPET can be used to provide individualized objective cut-off values aimed at minimizing PEM during exercise therapy and/or activities of daily living. Trial registration: DRKS, DRKS00032394. Registered 28 July 2023, https://drks.de/search/de/trial/DRKS00032394
7149: BACKGROUND: Persistent circulating SARS-CoV-2 spike protein has been proposed as a potential contributor to long-COVID pathophysiology. Whether administration of spike-targeting monoclonal antibodies is followed by changes in spike protein concentrations, autonomic receptor autoantibodies, or clinical outcomes remains uncertain. METHODS: In this prospective, non-randomized observational study, 21 participants were enrolled. Ten immunodeficient patients with long-COVID-associated ME/CFS and detectable circulating spike protein received Tixagevimab/Cilgavimab for SARS-CoV-2 pre-exposure prophylaxis. One patient subsequently withdrew consent, leaving nine patients for paired baseline and 30-day follow-up analyses. Eleven healthy individuals with previous SARS-CoV-2 infection but without long COVID provided descriptive reference data and were not considered an efficacy control group. RESULTS: β1-adrenergic receptor autoantibody concentrations decreased from 26.8 ± 18.2 to 21.2 ± 14.7 U/ml (unadjusted p = 0.003). No statistically significant changes were observed for β2-adrenergic or M3/M4-muscarinic receptor autoantibodies. Median spike protein concentrations changed from 63 pg/ml (IQR 9-127) to 26 pg/ml (IQR 10-120; p = 0.63), with individual decreases observed in five of nine patients. None of the assessed clinical outcomes changed significantly at group level. Changes in spike protein concentrations were not significantly correlated with changes in the assessed autonomic receptor autoantibodies. CONCLUSION: Tixagevimab/Cilgavimab administration was followed by a nominally significant within-patient reduction in β1-adrenergic receptor autoantibody concentrations, but not by conclusive changes in circulating spike protein or clinical outcomes. These findings are preliminary and hypothesis-generating. The small sample size, non-randomized design, brief 30-day follow-up, inclusion of only immunodeficient patients, and absence of an untreated disease-matched control group preclude conclusions regarding therapeutic efficacy.
7150: Poster presented at the HSE Integrated Healthcare Conference 2026
7151: Abstract Post-COVID Syndrome (PCS) presents with persistent symptoms such as fatigue, muscle weakness, and cognitive impairments, which often impact quality of life. This study determines handgrip strength (HGS) using a digital hand dynamometer as an objective measure of muscle function in PCS, aiming to assess its utility in symptom quantification and explore its relationship with endothelial dysfunction (ED) and inflammatory markers. In a cohort of 102 patients with PCS (77 women and 25 men), 62 of 101 classified patients (61.4%) fulfilled criteria for myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS). HGS parameters, including mean HGS, fatigability, and recovery, were assessed. Patients with ME/CFS exhibited lower mean HGS ( p = 0.031), greater fatigability ( p = 0.042), and poorer recovery ( p = 0.048) compared with patients without ME/CFS. Furthermore, HGS parameters were significantly correlated with PCS severity and patient-reported outcome measures (including COVID-19 Yorkshire Rehabilitation Scale, PCS Severity Score and Fatigue Severity Scale). A gender-specific analysis revealed associations between HGS and ferritin in males (r = 0.42, p = 0.036) and thrombocyte levels inversely related to muscle recovery (r = − 0.43, p = 0.030), potentially indicating microvascular compromise. Elevated intercellular adhesion molecule-1 (ICAM-1) levels were observed in patients with reduced recovery and VEGF was inversely correlated with fatigability in ME/CFS patients (r = − 0.26, p = 0.044), suggesting that ED is involved in PCS-related muscle dysfunction. Anti-S1 IgG titers correlated negatively with HGS in females (r = − 0.24, p = 0.040), suggesting a potential role of viral persistence in muscle impairment. These findings underscore the role of HGS in PCS assessment, revealing phenotype- and gender-specific impairments and highlighting the need for further research into ED pathways and targeted rehabilitation strategies to enhance PCS management.
7152: BACKGROUND: Cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) has been used for chronic fatigue syndrome (CFS), but previous studies have shown inconsistencies and divergent long-term outcomes. This study aims to assess the effectiveness of CBT in improving fatigue, physical functioning, and psychological health in patients with CFS. METHODS: We searched PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, and the Cochrane Library from their inception to March 2025. Studies designed as randomized controlled trials, enrolling patients diagnosed with CFS who received CBT as a treatment intervention delivered face-to-face, in groups, or online were included. The primary outcome was the fatigue score, and the secondary outcomes were the physical function score, psychological outcomes, and adverse events. The quality of the included studies was evaluated using the Cochrane Assessment Tool for Risk of Bias Version 2 (RoB 2; The Cochrane Collaboration). Heterogeneity was detected by subgroup analysis and sensitivity analysis. RESULTS: Fifteen randomized controlled trials with 2270 participants were involved. Meta-analysis demonstrated that CBT yielded significant posttreatment improvements across key outcomes. Fatigue severity was notably reduced, as measured by the Chalder Fatigue Questionnaire (standardized mean difference [SMD] = -0.44, 95% confidence interval [CI]: -0.57--0.32) and the Checklist Individual Strength (SMD = -0.88, 95% CI: -1.16--0.60). Physical functioning (physical function subscale of the Short Form Health Survey-36) subscale also improved significantly (SMD = 0.32, 95% CI: 0.23-0.41). Psychological health benefits were evident through reduced Symptom Checklist 90 (SMD = -0.44, 95% CI: -0.62--0.26) and specific decreases in anxiety (Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale-anxiety scale: SMD = -0.28, 95% CI: -0.46--0.10) and depression (Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale-depression scale: SMD = -0.27, 95% CI: -0.45--0.09). Follow-up analyses confirmed sustained benefits: short-term (≤ 6 months) showed continued fatigue reduction (Chalder Fatigue Questionnaire: SMD = -0.29, 95% CI: -0.55--0.03) and improved physical function (physical function subscale of the Short Form Health Survey-36: SMD = 0.31, 95% CI: 0.03-0.58); long-term (6-24 months) maintained fatigue relief (SMD = -0.35, 95% CI: -0.50--0.19) and functional gains (SMD = 0.21, 95% CI: 0.06-0.37). Safety analysis showed no statistically significant difference in adverse event rates (odds ratio = 0.61, 95% CI: 0.36-1.01, P = .060). CONCLUSION: Based on our results, CBT may be an effective option for CFS, but further research is warranted.
7153: PURPOSE: Healthcare professionals (HCPs) treating patients with chronic fatigue syndrome (CFS) work within a contested field marked by uncertainty. This study explored how HCPs using psychologically and behaviourally informed approaches to CFS understood therapeutic change and their role in facilitating recovery. METHODS: We used reflexive thematic analysis of two focus groups and three individual interviews with 16 HCPs from five professions, purposively sampled across clinical settings. Participants had at least two years' experience working with patients with CFS and represented diverse therapeutic and theoretical perspectives. RESULTS: The analysis was organised around four interrelated themes: (1) meeting patients in a "no-man's-land", (2) offering a new explanatory "map", (3) navigating by the map, and (4) maintaining trust in a contested field. HCPs described offering frameworks integrating biological, psychological, and social processes. Two overlapping orientations emphasised either stress, overload, and impaired regulation or maladaptive learning, perception, and self-sustaining symptom processes. Across orientations, validation and fostering agency were central. Embodied experiences of improvement were considered important for strengthening trust and confidence that change was possible. Competing illness narratives challenged trust. CONCLUSIONS: Participating HCPs described explanatory frameworks, their application in practice, therapeutic relationships, and patients' embodied experiences of improvement as interacting to make recovery conceivable.
7154: Standard drug electrophoresis, unlike intranasal electrophoresis, has a number of significant limitations. The aim of this study was to analyze domestic and foreign scientific experience in the use of intranasal electrophoresis in treatment and rehabilitation. The study material comprised publications presented in the English-language PubMed database, the Russian-language scientific electronic library eLibrary.Ru (RSCI), and other Internet sources. The analysis included domestic and foreign scientific studies and review articles from 1950 to the present. Articles were searched using the key phrases “эндоназальный электрофорез” (endonasal electrophoresis) and “интраназальный электрофорез” (intranasal electrophoresis). The search identified 103 sources, which were analyzed and structured. The areas of application of intranasal electrophoresis described in the analyzed publications are grouped into six groups: 1) diseases of the circulatory system (myocardial infarction, essential hypertension); 2) diseases of the respiratory system, including diseases of the ENT organs (tuberculosis, bronchial asthma, polyposis of the nose and paranasal sinuses, rhinopathy, rhinitis, rhinosinusitis, septal perforation, post-COVID-19 anosmia); 3) eye diseases (keratitis, neuritis, neuropathy and atrophy of the optic nerve, injuries of the adnexa of the eye, glaucoma, cataract, ocular tuberculosis, ophthalmopathies of various origins, age-related macular degeneration, uveitis); 4) diseases of the nervous system (consequences of traumatic brain injuries, autonomic dysfunction, consequences of stroke, tension headache, chronic fatigue syndrome, psychiatric disorders); 5) skin diseases (lichen planus, rosacea, perioral dermatitis); 6) other areas of application of intranasal electrophoresis (threatened preterm labor, rheographic studies, hypothalamic-autonomic-visceral syndrome, chromium intoxication, gastric and duodenal ulcer disease). In the analyzed publications, intranasal electrophoresis is most widely described as a method of treatment and rehabilitation for diseases of the respiratory system and diseases of the ear, nose, and throat, eye diseases, and diseases of the nervous system. In most publications, intranasal electrophoresis was considered not as the main and only treatment method, but as a component of complex therapy, as well as a method of drug administration.
7156: Background: The exact cause of chronic fatigue syndrome (CFS) is remained unclear, but increased oxidative stress has been reported in affected patients. Antioxidant supplementation helps reduce fatigue by minimizing oxidation of cellular substrates. Owing to its rich flavonoids content, ethanolic extract of Terminalia catappa Linn. leaves (EETCL) show strong antioxidant activity and may offers strong benefits against experimentally induced CFS. Objectives: The objective of the study is to evaluate the therapeutic potential of Terminalia catappa Linn. Leaves in prevention of chronic fatigue syndrome by forced swimming in rats. Methods: EETCL was prepared using Soxhlet extraction and investigated in Wistar albino rats. Animals were divided into five groups (n=6): Group I (naïve), Group II (stress control), Group III (standard, Imipramine HCl 20 mg/kg), Group IV and V (EETCL 250 mg/kg and 500 mg/kg respectively). All groups except the naïve group were subjected to daily forced swimming (15 min) for 28 days to induce CFS. Test and standard drugs were administered 30 min prior to swimming. Behavioural and Biochemical models were used for evaluation. Statistical significance was analysed using one-way ANOVA. Results: Treatment with EETCL (250 mg/kg and 500 mg/kg) and imipramine HCL (20mg/kg) resulted in statistically significant reduction in anxiety and duration of immobility. And there was significant increase in loco-motor activity and muscle grip strength when compared to stress control group. The brain homogenate showed significant decrease in Malondialdehyde level and enhanced in catalase level were seen in EETCL and Imipramine treated group when compared to stress control group. Conclusion: The study confirms that ethanolic extract of Terminalia catappa Linn. has protective effect against experimentally induced CFS. Keywords: Chronic fatigue syndrome; forced swim test; oxidative stress; Malondialdehyde; Anti-oxidants; Imipramine HCL.
7157: Introduction Myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS) is a debilitating multisystem disorder associated with immune dysregulation yet lacks definitive biomarkers or effective therapies. Acute immune perturbations may transiently modulate disease manifestations. Methods We report the case of a female patient in her 60s with severe, long-standing ME/CFS who experienced changes in symptom following administration of recombinant zoster vaccine (RZV; Shingrix). Peripheral blood mononuclear cells were analyzed pre- and post-vaccination using flow cytometry, with comparison to a female healthy control. Plasma galectin-9 (Gal-9) levels were quantified by ELISA. Results Both RZV doses were associated with rapid, transient remission of symptoms, including improved sleep, cognition, pain, mobility, and respiratory function, followed by relapse. Immunologically, pre-vaccination profiling revealed elevated monocytes, increased CD71 + erythroid cells, and features of T cell exhaustion marked by Gal-9/PD-1 co-expression and impaired cytokine responses. Post-vaccination, monocyte frequency decreased, Gal-9 + /PD-1 + T cells were reduced, and NK cell degranulation improved, indicating partial restoration of immune function. Conclusion This case demonstrates that immune stimulation via RZV may transiently reverse immune dysfunction and improve clinical symptoms in ME/CFS. These findings support a role for reversible immune exhaustion in disease pathogenesis and highlight potential avenues for biomarker development and therapeutic intervention.
7158: The detection of low-abundance viral RNA in chronic or persistent infections remains a major challenge in virology, constrained by the sensitivity and specificity of traditional methods. One such infection, chronic enterovirus (EV) infection, has been proposed as a potential underlying factor in Myalgic Encephalomyelitis (ME), although this hypothesis remains debated. Supporting evidence for EVs as a viral trigger includes historical spatiotemporal overlaps between ME outbreaks and poliomyelitis epidemics, frequent reports of “flu-like” illness at disease onset, seasonal outbreaks patterns, and serological findings. To address the problem of EV detection, we developed CATCH-EVseq, an ultra-sensitive platform built on the CATCH framework. By integrating high-throughput sequencing with cDNA capture using 49,847 probes targeting 3410 EV genomes, CATCH-EVseq achieved a detection limit in artificially created samples as low as one copy in a microgram of RNA for two out of three biological replicates. Additionally, spike-in controls allow for rigorous validation of the capture and sequencing throughout the CATCH-EVseq procedure. When applied to a small number of blood samples from both ME patients and healthy controls, CATCH-EVseq detected no EV RNA, either in direct assays or after in vitro viral amplification. While these results do not support the presence of circulating EV RNA in the blood of individuals with ME, they do not rule out persistent infection in other tissues or organs. Critically, CATCH-EVseq establishes a robust, ultra-sensitive framework for future investigations of low-level EV persistence in biopsies, post-mortem tissues, or other clinical contexts where chronic enterovirus infection is suspected.
7159: This manuscript explores the ways in which the future of long COVID was both always circumscribed and expertly managed. When long COVID emerged, it was immediately recognized as a contested condition, and as such, was destined to carry the baggage of many complex forms of suffering that came before it. However, those suffering from long COVID managed to harness the energy of the pandemic crisis to produce new opportunities and new possible futures, not only for themselves, but for others with contested conditions. These dimensions are examined through a close look at an interesting alliance that formed between those suffering from long COVID and those diagnosed with myalgic encephalomyelitis / chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS), most prominently in the United States and United Kingdom; how this alliance has been both fruitful and challenging; and the roots of dualism that underlie widespread ontological and moral assumptions within medicine.
7160: It is important to determine whether the persistent cognitive and fatigue complaints, as part of post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC), are associated with underlying patterns and specific symptoms clusters. Therefore, the aim of the present study was to investigate symptom clusters and clinical phenotypes in PASC. We included n = 153 individuals (53 years old, 66% female, 2 years post SARS-CoV-2 infection) categorized into groups with (n = 88) and without (n = 65) PASC, defined by severe fatigue and concentration problems using validated cut-offs. Symptom clusters (i.e., component loadings and component scores) were identified using principal component analyses (PCA, eigenvalue[EV]>1.0), using clinical, somatic, coping and sleep factors, symptom severity, neuropsychological and physical tests (totalling 19 tests and questionnaires). We then used logistic regression techniques on (participant-level) component scores (standardized) to investigate associations with PASC. Finally, K-means clustering methods to identify clinical phenotypes. Analyses were adjusted for age, sex, education, nationality and time since infection. PCA identified 5 components, explaining 70% of the variance. We labelled these components as follows: (1) PEM, ME/CFS and sleep symptoms, coping factors (EV = 7.0, 36.9% variance), (2) information-processing speed (EV = 2.5, 13.3%), (3) executive functioning (EV = 1.5, 8.0%, (4) physical performance (EV = 1.2, 6.5%), (5) somatic comorbidities and hospital admission (EV = 1.0, 5.5%). Logistic regression showed that only the first component scores (Odds ratio [95% confidence interval] = 97.1 [16.5-570.3], p 0.05), associated with PASC. Cluster analysis revealed two distinct clinical phenotypes among individuals with severe chronic fatigue: one marked by physical impairment and the other by diminished cognitive performance. Consistent with existing literature, we confirmed that PASC is a heterogeneous syndrome marked by extensive, interrelated symptoms. Notably, we identified specific cognitive and physical clinical phenotypes. These findings are important for future targeted diagnosis and treatment.
7162: BACKGROUND: Myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS) is a complex illness lacking objective diagnostic biomarkers and clear pathophysiological understanding. Patients exhibit immune dysregulation and chronic inflammation reminiscent of aging phenotypes, yet the role of myeloid cell senescence in this disease remains unexplored. METHODS: A stepwise integrative transcriptomic and computational strategy was employed. Differentially expressed genes were identified from the bulk transcriptomic dataset GSE14577. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis was performed to identify key modules correlated with the ME/CFS phenotype. Candidate genes were obtained by intersecting these modules with aging-related genes from the GenAge database. Core hub genes were further selected using LASSO regression and random forest machine learning algorithms. Cell type-specific expression was mapped using single-cell RNA sequencing data GSE214283, and functional validation was conducted via siRNA knockdown in a THP-1 cell senescence model. RESULTS: Integrative analysis identified HMGCR and SGK1 as core hub genes. Functional enrichment analysis revealed that candidate genes were enriched in pathways related to cellular senescence and inflammation. Single-cell transcriptomics analysis suggested that SGK1 expression was enriched in myeloid cell populations, including monocytes and neutrophils, in individuals with ME/CFS, whereas HMGCR showed a broader expression pattern. Single-gene GSEA indicated that SGK1 was associated with autophagy and lysosomal function. In vitro experiments showed that SGK1 expression was significantly upregulated in D-galactose-induced senescent THP-1 cells, and SGK1 knockdown markedly reduced the mRNA expression levels of senescence markers p16, p21, and p53. CONCLUSION: This study identifies SGK1 as a candidate molecule associated with myeloid cell senescence-related alterations in ME/CFS. Integrated transcriptomic, single-cell, and experimental analyses suggest a potential link between SGK1 expression and aging-associated immune alterations. However, further validation in primary ME/CFS-derived immune cells and clinical cohorts is required to determine the biological significance and clinical relevance of SGK1.
7163: BACKGROUND: Long/post COVID and related conditions such as myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome, postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome and post-vaccination syndrome are associated with persistent functional impairments and are met with care structures in Germany that are difficult to navigate. OBJECTIVE: The rapid scoping review offers an insight into care structures, capacities, access, care pathways and gaps in care for these patient groups in the German healthcare system. It also takes into account patient and care provider perspectives. METHODS: The study follows the recommendations of the Joanna Briggs Institute and the PRISMA ScR checklist for conducting (rapid) scoping reviews. A MEDLINE search was conducted from 2020 onwards with predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria for evidence sources related to care in Germany. RESULTS: 44 evidence sources were included. General practitioners and paediatricians act as the first point of contact. Specialised outpatient clinics and rehabilitation facilities take on complex diagnostics and patient treatment. Care networks are rare. Navigating the healthcare system is characterised by information gaps, unclear responsibilities and long waiting times, so that those affected often organise their own care. Some report stigmatisation, misdiagnoses and stressful activation recommendations despite the risk of post exertional malaise. CONCLUSION: Care is unevenly accessible, poorly coordinated and only limitedly evidence based. Shared knowledge and case databases, training, better diagnostic tools and robust efficacy studies are needed to improve access, management and safety of long/post COVID care.
7164: Abstract Background The aetiology of Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome (ME/CFS) remains unknown, and no validated disease models, biomarkers, or effective treatments are currently available. Debilitating fatigue and post-exertional malaise, together with chronic muscle pain and weakness, are hallmarks of ME/CFS. Indeed, skeletal muscle from people with ME/CFS has been reported to exhibit signs of damage and mitochondrial alterations, although the underlying biological processes remain poorly understood. This study used patient-derived induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived myogenic progenitor (MP) cells to investigate ME/CFS-associated transcriptomic differences and identify potential drug-repurposing candidates. Methods MP cells were generated from iPSCs derived from people with ME/CFS and healthy controls and characterised. RNA sequencing was performed to compare transcriptomic profiles between ME/CFS and control MPs ( n = 6 and n = 7, respectively). Differentially expressed genes and pathways were identified using DESeq2 and gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA), followed by drug-repurposing analysis using the Library of Integrated Network-based Cellular Signatures (LINCS2) database and supporting literature review. Results RNA sequencing identified seven differentially expressed genes at adjusted p < 0.05, including MIR205HG , FEZF1 , HLA-DMB , SLC1A2 , SYT13 , GALNT4 , and SLC2A14 . Pathway analysis identified 73 significantly enriched pathways, 96% of which were downregulated in ME/CFS MPs, including pathways related to cell-cycle regulation, DNA replication, immune responses, and muscle cytoskeletal regulation. In contrast, branched-chain amino acid degradation was upregulated. LINCS2-based inverse signature matching followed by literature review identified 21 prioritised drug-repurposing candidates with potential relevance to ME/CFS. These included approved drugs such as leflunomide, melatonin, and midodrine, spanning pharmacological domains related to immune, neurological, autonomic, and vascular processes and warranting further experimental evaluation. Conclusions Patient-derived iPSC-MPs provide a useful platform for investigating ME/CFS-associated transcriptional differences in a muscle-relevant cell type. The findings support further investigation of skeletal muscle-related molecular processes in ME/CFS and provide a basis for experimental evaluation of computationally prioritised drug-repurposing candidates.
7165: Background Long COVID is a multisystem disease that affects approximately 10% of people after a SARS-CoV-2 infection. In the absence of curative treatment, high-quality clinical treatment trials are urgently needed for long COVID. There is significant overlap between long COVID and other infection-associated chronic conditions, in particular myalgic encephalomyelitis. As such, trial design for long COVID can benefit from prior experience in this field. In this review we explore outcome measures in long COVID and myalgic encephalomyelitis clinical trials to survey current practices, and provide recommendations for future clinical trials. PubMed and Clinicaltrials.gov were searched for clinical trials on long COVID and myalgic encephalomyelitis that featured a biomedical intervention. 37 myalgic encephalomyelitis and 68 long COVID trials were identified that used 397 outcome measures in total. We then critically assessed the relevance of these outcome measures for patients. Conclusion Long COVID trial design could be improved by incorporating outcomes that address important symptom clusters such as post-exertional malaise, dysautonomia and mast cell activation. Clinical assessments, physical tests and biomarkers can supplement patient reported outcome measure data, if safety, feasibility and applicability are carefully considered. Lastly, safety of the intervention is rarely adequately evaluated. We recommend a concerted effort to include patient input at all steps of clinical trial design, execution and evaluation.
7166: Background.— The diagnosis of chronic fatigue syndrome (CFS) is made on the basis of general fatigue and post-exertional malaise, unrefreshing sleep, cognitive impairment, and orthostatic-related symptoms persisting for at least 6 months. CFS occurs in the setting of some hematological diseases, at the time of chemotherapy or radiotherapy during the treatment of certain tumors, and because of some autoimmune diseases and viral infections such as COVID-19. CFS is often a diagnostic dilemma, given the varying nonspecific symptoms and lack of physical findings. A reliable test for physical disability is treadmill exercise. Biomarkers thus far have not been identified. Methods.— Results of careful examination of a cohort of 50 cases who presented with symptoms of CFS were analyzed in an observational study. The examinations consisted of laboratory analyses including measurements of the cytokines interleukin-6 (IL-6) and tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α) in serum and treadmill exercise testing. Results were grouped according to individuals with normal versus increased cytokine values. Results.— In total, 18 of the 50 cases had increased levels of IL-6 or TNF-α. They were distinguished by reduced physical ability as measured by treadmill exercise testing, with a reduction to 82% in the cases with increased cytokine levels, versus 97% of cases with normal cytokine levels. This was found to be statistically significant by parametric and nonparametric statistical tests. A Spearman rank test showed significant correlations among IL-6, TNF-α, duration of CFS, and ergometer results. Conclusion.— Elevations of IL-6 and/or TNF-α were associated with CFS of various origins, including autoimmune diseases, hematological diseases, long-COVID syndromes, or tumors in remission. Determination of serum levels of these cytokines can serve as a valuable biomarker to identify individuals with active fatigue syndromes.
7167: Background Light is a major environmental factor regulating circadian rhythms, sleep- wake cycles, and mood-related behaviors. Patients with Myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS) often experience circadian disruption and poor sleep quality, which severely compromise their quality of life; however, the relationship between light exposure and illness severity remains largely unknown. Methods An observational cross-sectional cohort secondary study used collected data from 100 ME/CFS patients and 56 healthy controls to explore the impact of spontaneous light exposure on multidimensional health status and circulating biochemical parameters. Demographic and clinical features were assessed using validated patient-reported outcome measures. Light intensity, wrist temperature, and physical activity were continuously monitored at home over one week using wrist-worn actigraphy. Light intensity during predefined intervals and rhythmic variables of light cycle were calculated. Principal component analysis (PCA) was applied to reduce dimensionality of light variables. Multivariable analysis was performed adjusting for age, sex, body mass index, and physical activity. Results Following PCA of the light patterns, two components emerged across groups with high consistency: PC1 (explaining 61.7% of the total variance) reflected higher daytime light and rhythm stability, and PC2 (explaining 16.1%) represented nocturnal/early-morning light and rhythm instability. In ME/CFS patients, light variables were more extensively associated with clinical outcomes measures (FIS-40, PSQI and SF-36) than in healthy controls (all p < 0.05). Furthermore, PC2 was associated with higher levels of VCAM-1 and triglycerides, and lower serotonin concentrations (all p < 0.05). Four distinct light patterns were identified based on PCA scores: nocturnal light, healthy, adverse, and low diurnal light. ME/CFS patients exhibiting the healthy light pattern showed significantly lower fatigue, fewer sleep complaints, reduced autonomic dysfunction, and higher quality of life compared to those with the adverse light pattern (all p < 0.05). No significant differences were observed among healthy controls. Conclusions Light exposure patterns show distinct associations with symptom variability in ME/CFS compared to healthy controls. More stable daytime light appears to relate to better symptom profiles, whereas irregular exposure and nocturnal light are linked to poorer health outcomes. Although causality cannot be inferred, these findings highlight light exposure as a potentially modifiable, non-invasive target for behavioral interventions aimed at improving the quality of life in ME/CFS, representing a promising emerging for future translational research.
7168: Background Chronic fatigue syndrome is characterized by multiple co-occurring physical, cognitive, sleep, and emotional symptoms. Traditional symptom cluster analysis identifies patterns of symptom co-occurrence but does not clarify the relative importance of individual symptoms or the connections between symptom clusters. Symptom network analysis may complement this approach by identifying core and bridge symptoms. Objective To investigate the symptom clusters and structural characteristics of symptom networks in patients with chronic fatigue syndrome, thereby providing a basis for developing targeted strategies for managing symptoms. Methods A convenience sampling method was used to enroll 214 patients with chronic fatigue syndrome. Data were collected using a demographic questionnaire and an adapted version of the Chinese Memorial Symptom Assessment Scale. Data were analyzed using SPSS 27.0. Symptom clusters were extracted using principal component analysis (PCA) with varimax rotation, and a symptom network was constructed in R to calculate expected influence and bridge expected influence, thereby identifying core and bridge symptoms. Results The three most common symptoms, in descending order, were fatigue (100.00%), difficulty concentrating (90.7%), and feeling drowsy (86.9%). A total of six symptom clusters were identified: Emotional-Sleep Symptom cluster, Fatigue Symptom cluster, Physical symptom cluster, Self-Image symptom cluster, Gastrointestinal symptom cluster, and Neurological symptom cluster, with a cumulative variance contribution of 63.114%. Fatigue had the highest expected influence (rEI = 1.541), followed by worrying (rEI = 1.169); fatigue (rbEI = 0.430), pain (rbEI = 0.363), and difficulty sleeping (rbEI = 0.309) were the primary bridge symptoms. Conclusion Patients with chronic fatigue syndrome exhibit co-occurring symptoms and connections across symptom clusters. Fatigue serves as both a core symptom and a bridging symptom, while worrying, difficulty sleeping, and pain are also critical areas of focus in symptom management. Clinically, fatigue should be prioritized for assessment and management, while concurrently conducting comprehensive evaluations of mood, sleep, and pain. Individualized management plans should be developed based on the characteristics of symptom clusters and symptom networks to alleviate the symptom burden in patients with chronic fatigue syndrome and improve their quality of life.
